Arjun / Irene — quick technical note from the first-pass triage.

What we see in the logs: intermittent TLS session teardown originating from the controller egress path, spaced at ~5–7 minute intervals. Packet captures show a burst of ICMP fragmentation-needed messages correlated with the controller keepalive windows. That points to an MTU/egress-path fragmentation regression introduced when we enforced the stricter egress ACL.

Snippet (redacted):
[2028-03-10T03:22:14Z] controller-01 TLS_ALERT (peer initiated) session_id=... src=10.2.88.11 dst=54.38.21.9
[2028-03-10T03:22:15Z] icmp: fragmentation-needed mtu=1400 path=eth0

Proposed immediate mitigations (tested on a staging cluster):
1) Re-open port range 49152–49175 for controller telemetry to avoid forced path MTU discovery failures.
2) Spin a lightweight proxy that sets DF=0 for keepalive packets for affected subnets (short term).
3) We'll prepare a targeted patch to the egress rule handling that preserves the pooling improvement but avoids aggressive path MTU-dependent behavior.

I've added the mitigation runbook to the attachments (mitigation-runbook-v1.md). If you want us to flip the ACL now, give the go-ahead and Naomi's team will coordinate a controlled change window with your network team.

—Marcus

Sanjay / Arjun — following our bridge and the controlled mitigation window, here's a concise post-incident summary and next steps. Attaching the postmortem draft and the diagnostic bundle for your internal review.

Incident timeline (high level):
- 2028-03-10 03:10 UTC — Controller release 2.14.0 deploy (pooling + egress filter change).
- 2028-03-10 03:18 UTC — First observed control-channel TLS tear during keepalive. Intermittent repeats during peak windows through 2028-03-11.
- 2028-03-12 10:00 PST — Bridge call with CardioSync. Identified ICMP fragmentation traces implicating egress ACLs + path MTU interactions.
- 2028-03-13 02:40 UTC — Naomi's team temporarily relaxed egress filter for affected subnets; observed stabilization.
- 2028-03-15 23:00 UTC — Patch v2.14.1 rolled to controller fleet that preserves pooling improvement and fixes ACL semantics.
- 2028-03-16 03:00 UTC — Observed full recovery with no recurrent TLS tears for 72h.

Scope & data exposure:
- The control plane carries metadata (node identifiers, heartbeat, session state) but not application payloads. We confirmed there was no customer PII or application payload in the control-plane packets during the incident.

Root cause (short):
- A tightened egress ACL change in 2.14.0 unintentionally blocked ephemeral ports used during path MTU discovery, causing fragmentation-related TLS disconnects for certain network paths.

Remediation & follow-ups:
1) We released 2.14.1 with corrected ACL handling and an automated regression test for PMTU-related flows.
2) Added a post-deploy network compatibility gate in the CI that runs PMTU scenarios on representative partner topologies.
3) Shared mitigation-runbook-v1.md for temporary ACL relax and proxy options if you want conservative controls.
4) We'll deliver the final postmortem and a compliance evidence bundle (SOC2 excerpt and audit logs) via a secure drive link by EOD Monday.

Attachments: postmortem-draft-CardioSync-20280316.pdf (draft), diagnostic-bundle-20280312.tar.gz, mitigation-runbook-v1.md
